liam: ran an nsys capture on 8xA100 (fp16) with seq_len=4096 and saw ~120ms gaps inside the tensor-parallel stages, looks like all-reduce overlap is not happening as expected
liam: command I used: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl -o trace_async_kernels ./bin/serve --config=config/prod-trace.yaml`
sarah: can you paste the timeline snapshot? perfetto link or screenshot helps :eyes:
liam: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 (uploaded) — main suspect is a kernel selector flip around step 1200 where we pick a slower kernel for small sequence remnants
tom: interesting, last week we changed the kernel selection heuristic to prefer cudnn fused kernels for lengths > 1024, maybe edge-case at 4096 windows with remainder chunks\perf-bot: [autobot] perf-regression alert: median token latency +16% in nightly after kernel-selector PR #342\alex: I see two patterns in the nsys: 1) NCCL all-reduce starts, then stalls waiting on CUDA streams for ~80-150ms; 2) frequent small kernel launches between reductions — could be KV cache eviction/warmup\liam: KV cache config: ttl_items=65536, retire_stride=128. When batcher emits variable-length sequences we sometimes evict and repopulate CP cache, causing short kernels to run and break overlap\sarah: can you post the nvprof/ncu kernel table? even a top10 list would help\liam: pasted top kernels: `attention_fwd_v2` 38% time, `kv_restore` 12%, `allreduce_nccl` 18%, `small_transpose` 9%\tom: `kv_restore` spikes align with particular requests that have large prefix + short new tokens — our prefix-KV merging path does a memcpy-heavy fallback\alex: hypothesis: when kernel selector switches to a non-batched attention (because remainder < 32), we pay both a small kernel and block NCCL overlap — serialization effect\sarah: quick mitigation: adjust batching heuristic to avoid creating small remainder shards. e.g. set batcher.min_chunk=32 and prefer pad-to-chunk over emit-remainder\liam: tested locally: changing min_chunk 16->32 reduced small kernel counts by ~45% and improved overlap; p95 improved ~9% on the trace machine\perf-bot: note: make sure to run multi-node nccl tests; local single-node overlap may hide cross-node serialization\tom: small snippet of the config I changed: ```batcher:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  min_chunk_size: 32
  pad_small_remainders: true
```\alex: also check nccl version and CUDA driver; we saw better async progress on 2.12.12 vs older stacks\liam: next steps: 1) run an nsys job with PR patch (batcher change + force kernel selector bias) across 4 nodes; 2) capture nvtx regions from serving runtime to correlate stream-scheduling; 3) add histogram of small kernel durations to perf dashboard\sarah: can someone run the 4-node repro this afternoon? I can help with collecting perfetto links and converting to flamegraphs\tom: I'll queue the job on the internal perf cluster (8xA100 per node) — will attach nsys and perfetto output here when done\alex: FYI I briefly profiled with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` to isolate ordering: things serialized and latency jumped as expected, so it's scheduling overlap problem not a pure NCCL bug\liam: thanks — I'll open a short-lived feature flag to roll out min_chunk=32 to canary and watch p95; if stable we can make the kernel selector prefer the fast fused path for the remainder pattern\sarah: perfect. also flagging for release notes: "mitigate all-reduce overlap regression by batching remainder padding and KV warmup reductions" :thumbsup:
liam: thanks team, will post nsys + perfetto links in this thread once the 4-node run finishes\perf-bot: [autobot] scheduled nightly regression comparison with new canary config\liam: (edit) 4-node run started at 2026-03-18T16:12:00Z, PID 4521 — expected to finish ~25m
